[[File:Renate Loll.jpg|thumb|Renate Loll]]
'''Renate Loll''' (born 19 June 1962, [[Aachen]])<ref>[https://profs.library.uu.nl/index.php/profrec/getprofdata/1304/1/1/0 Prof.dr. R. Loll (1962 - )] at the ''Catalogus Professorum Academiæ Rheno-Traiectinæ''</ref> is a German physicist. She is a  Professor in Theoretical Physics at the Institute for Mathematics, Astrophysics and Particle Physics of the [[Radboud University]] in [[Nijmegen, Netherlands]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.hef.ru.nl/~rloll/Web/title/title.html|title=Renate Loll|last=Müller|first=A.|date=2004|website=www.hef.ru.nl}}</ref>  She previously worked at the Institute for Theoretical Physics of [[Utrecht University]]. She received her Ph.D. from [[Imperial College London|Imperial College]], London, in 1989. In 2001 she joined the permanent staff of the ITP, after spending several years at the [[Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics]] in Golm, [[Germany]].  With [[Jan Ambjørn]] and Polish physicist [[Jerzy Jurkiewicz]] she helped develop a new approach to  nonperturbative [[quantum gravity|quantization of gravity]], that of [[Causal dynamical triangulation|Causal Dynamical Triangulations]].

She has been a member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] since 2015.<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members/13683 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160210204721/https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members/13683 |title=Renate Loll |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |archive-date=10 February 2016 |accessdate=10 February 2016}}</ref>
